chunks: We were informed by Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from his father, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: 'Name to me one of the virtuous ones (I mean the Qa'im).' He said: 'His name is my name.' I said: 'Will he walk in the manner of Muhammad?' He said: 'Far off, far off, O Zurara, he will not walk in his manner.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, why?' He said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah walked among his ummah with leniency; he would win people over (with kindness), whereas the Qa'im walks with killing; for that he was ordered in the Book that is with him to walk with killing and not to ask anyone to repent. Woe to whoever opposes him.'

key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qa'im, referring to the Awaited Imam Muhammad ibn al-Hasan
key_terms.الْكِتَابِ: The Book, referring to the divine decree or scripture accompanying the Imam
key_terms.بِالْقَتْلِ: With killing/sword, describing the Qa'im's method
key_terms.بِالْمَنِّ: With leniency/favor, describing the Prophet's approach
key_terms.وَلَا يَسْتَتِيبَ أَحَدًا: And not asking anyone to repent, indicating immediate execution of opponents
key_terms.يَتَأَلَّفُ النَّاسَ: Winning people over (kindly), a specific prophetic method

ai.seo_question: How does the governance style of the Qa'im differ from that of Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir distinguishes the Qa'im’s eschatological governance from the Prophet’s earthly mission, noting that while the Prophet employed *talfif* (conciliatory diplomacy) to unite the community, the Qa'im rules with decisive force (*al-qatl*) as commanded in his divine Book. This contrast highlights the shift from a period of gradual spiritual consolidation to one of immediate, uncompromising justice where opponents are executed without the usual offer of repentance (*istitab*), fulfilling the divine decree for the establishment of true monotheism.
